title: CONFESS IN WHAT WAY YOU HAVE SINNED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'When anyone becomes aware that they are guilty in any of these matters, they must confess in what way they have sinned.'" - Lev 5:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the most practical verses in Leviticus, and it turns on four words: in what way they have sinned.

Not a general confession. Not "Lord, forgive me for everything." God asks for specifics. Name it.

There is a reason for this. Vague confession keeps us comfortable. It lets us acknowledge guilt in the abstract while never actually looking at what we did. We can say "I'm a sinner like everyone else" all day and never once face the particular unkindness, the particular dishonesty, the particular thing we would hate to say out loud.

Specific confession is harder. It is also the only kind that changes anything.

John writes, If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins (1 Jn 1:9) — and the word he uses means to say the same thing as God says about it. Not to minimise it, rename it, or file it under a softer heading. To agree with God about what it actually was.

Try this today. Instead of praying "forgive my sins," name one. Say what you did, without the explanation you usually attach to it.

That is where forgiveness stops being a doctrine and starts being an experience.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do my confessions stay general so that I never have to look closely?
2. What is one specific thing I need to name honestly before God today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I have hidden behind vague words. Today I name before You what I actually did, and I ask for Your mercy. Amen.
